data.name: Jule
data.gender_notes: Jule is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Germanic origin: derived from the root 'juhla' meaning 'feast' or 'rejoice'. The name Jule has been used as a short form of Juliana or Julieanne, both derived from the Latin 'Julia'. The name Jule carries the meaning “Youthful, Soft” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Jule usually hope their child will grow to embody youthful, soft and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the joy and merriment of the Christian faith.
data.etymology: Jule belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Youthful, Soft.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jule total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_hebrew.name: ג'ול
in_hebrew.long_meaning: ג'ול הוא שם שמקורו בשם העברי 'יוֹאֵל', שפירושו 'יהוה הוא אלוהים' או 'הוא שיחזיר לאלוהים'. השם ג'ול הוא גרסה קצרה של יואל, שנמצא בספרי התנך. הוא משויך לנביא יואל, שחזה את בוא הרוח הקודש. השם מופיע גם בברית החדשה, ומשמעותו רוחניות, קשר לאלוהים.

in_greek.name: Γιουλ
in_greek.long_meaning: Γιουλ είναι η σύντομη μορφή του ονόματος Ιωήλ (Yō'ēl), που σημαίνει «ο Θεός είναι Θεός» ή «απευθυνόμενος στον Θεό». Στο Χρηστικό κείμενο, το όνομα Γιουλ συνδέεται με τον προφήτη Ιωήλ, που ανέφερε την έλευση του Αγίου Πνεύματος. Το όνομα Γιουλ έχει βαθιά πνευματική σημασία και δείχνει την σχέση με το Θείο.

in_latin.name: Jule
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Jule derivatur ex hebraico 'Yō'ēl', quod significat 'Deus est Deus' vel 'Reductio ad Deum'. In traditione christiana, Jule est forma abbreviata nominis prophetae Ioel, qui praenuntiavit adventum Spiritus Sancti. Nomen hoc habet significationem spiritualem et connexionem cum Divino.

in_english.name: Jule
in_english.meaning: Descended from God or God will prevail
in_english.long_meaning: The name Jule is derived from the Hebrew 'Yō'ēl', meaning 'God is God' or 'Jehovah is God'. It is associated with the prophet Joel in the Old Testament, who foretold the coming of the Holy Spirit. The name signifies spiritual descent from God, divine favor, and a strong connection to faith. Historically, it has been used across various Christian cultures, symbolizing devotion and piety.

data.cultural_impact: Jule is a rare and captivating name that transcends borders with its delightful meaning rooted in the Germanic tradition of celebration and joy. It has a warm and inviting tone, symbolizing not just festivities but an enthusiasm towards life. The name fosters a connection to the vibrant heritage of Germanic cultures and their emphasis on communal gatherings and cheerfulness.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Jule carries an innate connection to spirituality through its origins, as it is derived from the root 'juhla', which essentially means 'feast' or 'rejoice'. This name serves as a reminder of the joy and peace we find in the love and companionship of our fellow humans and the divine. As the name suggests, every moment of life is an opportunity to rejoice, to celebrate the simple pleasures of existence, and to cultivate a profound sense of connectedness to a higher power and to the sacred web of life. Every time one hears or utters the name Jule, it may inspire feelings of gratitude and hope, encouraging individuals to cherish their relationships and savour the small joys in their lives.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Jule derives from the Latin word 'julius,' meaning 'youthful' or 'downy-bearded.' In Christianity, it symbolizes the youthful spirit of Jesus Christ, whose birth we celebrate during the winter solstice. The name also embodies the spiritual growth and maturity one aspires to attain through faith.

biblical_reference.note: The name Jule originates from the prophet Joel, whose book is part of the Old Testament.

historical_references.reference: Julian calendar, named after the Roman emperor Julian the Apostate who attempted to reform the Roman calendar in the 4th century AD.
historical_references.context: Julian, a Christian convert, reintroduced the old Roman solar calendar with small modifications to bring it closer to the solar year, known as the Julian calendar.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Julian of Norwich, a Christian mystic, theologian, and anchorite in England in the 14th century. The name Jule carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Julian's most famous work, 'Revelations of Divine Love', is a collection of visions and reflections on the nature of God and the love of Christ, and she is considered one of the earliest women writers in the English language.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Jule' is of Scandinavian origin, derived from the Old Norse word for 'feast' or 'celebration'. In modern usage, the name is most commonly associated with the Christmas season, representing the festive atmosphere of the holiday. On social media, people often use the name 'Jule' in hashtags and captions to express the joy and excitement of the season (#Julemorgen, #Julenatte, #Julefest). In home decor, Jule-themed items such as candles, wreaths, and table runners are popular during the holiday season. In the food and beverage industry, Jule-inspired dishes and drinks, such as gløgg (mulled wine) and julekake (a traditional Norwegian cake), are enjoyed during the festive period.
